title: Numbers, Age, and Phone Numbers
summary: In this fun lesson, you will learn numbers from 1 to 100. You will also learn how to say your age and your phone number.

sections.p: First, let's learn the basic numbers. Numbers one to ten are easy: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. Numbers eleven to twenty are special words you need to memorize, like eleven, twelve, fifteen, and twenty.

To count by tens, we add 'ty' to the end. For example: thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, and one hundred. To make numbers like 35 or 42, just say the ten first and then the small number: thirty-five, forty-two.

sections.h: Saying Your Age and Phone Number
sections.p: To say how old you are, use the verb 'to be'. Say 'I am' and then your age. To share your phone number, say each digit one by one. For example, 555-1234 is five-five-five, one-two-three-four.

ex.mean: This is how you say your age.
This is how you share your phone number.

tip: Practice numbers by saying the prices of things you see when you go shopping! Also, say your phone number out loud every day to remember it.
